name: Central African Republic
flagName: Flag of the Central African Republic
summary: Blue, white, green and yellow horizontal bands crossed by a vertical red band, with a yellow star in the upper hoist. Designed by Barthélemy Boganda, it combines French colours with Pan-African ones.
origin: Barthélemy Boganda, leader of the independence movement, designed the flag for the autonomous Republic of Ubangi-Shari in 1958. He hoped it would serve a wider union of Central African states.
It was kept at independence in 1960 and through Jean-Bédel Bokassa's Central African Empire (1976–1979).

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Liberty; with white and red, the French colours.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Hope and faith; with yellow and red, the Pan-African colours.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood shared by all humanity, uniting Europe and Africa.

symbols.name: Star
symbols.description: A yellow five-pointed star in the upper hoist.
symbols.meaning: Independence and a guiding light toward the future.

history.label: National flag
history.note: Unchanged through the Central African Empire.

facts: Boganda said the red band symbolised the blood common to Europeans and Africans.
It is one of few national flags with both horizontal and vertical stripes crossing.
Boganda died in a plane crash in 1959, before independence.
clues: Blue, white, green and yellow bands crossed by a vertical red stripe, with a yellow star.
Its colours combine French and Pan-African palettes.
It survived unchanged through a self-proclaimed empire in the 1970s.
